visual_text: By 2013, a fall from under 2 metres was the commonest recorded cause of major trauma
England and Wales, trauma registry, 1990 and 2013
Fall from under 2 metres, 39 in 100 cases
Some of the change may reflect which hospitals reported and more CT scanning.
Kehoe et al., Emerg Med J 2015
Rib fractures: older people died more often
One US trauma centre, people admitted with rib fractures
Each extra broken rib was linked with higher odds of death. Data published in 2000.
We should look for head and chest injury after a low fall.
alt_text: Card 1: 1990 versus 2013 in England and Wales major trauma. 1990: road collisions 59 in 100 cases, average age 36. 2013: falls from under 2 metres 39 in 100, average age 54. A person icon grid shows 27 of 100 filled for about 1 in 4 cases over 75. Reporting and CT scanning may explain some change.
Card 2: bar chart per 100 people, one US trauma centre. Died: aged 65 and over 22, 18 to 64 10. Pneumonia: 31 versus 17. Crude figures. Judgement: look for head and chest injury after a low fall.
design_instructions: Two 4:5 light cards. Card 1 two panels (white 1990, mint 2013) with commonest cause and average age, 10x10 person icon array with 27 orange filled. Card 2 grouped horizontal bars, 0 to 40 axis, solid teal for 65 and over, hatched pale for 18 to 64; orange-rule judgement line. Claims C15-11-a, C15-11-b.
